summary: The first mismatch is the unported LEASH arm of apply.c:doapply: JavaScript stops at step 19 before the direction prompt. Recorded C applies an unused leash to an adjacent visible tame dog, reaches use_leash_core’s successful attach branch at step 20, sets both the monster mleashed flag and object leashmon ID, wakes the dog, and updates inventory.

source.branch: doapply dispatches a selected LEASH to use_leash; for an unused leash with fewer than MAXLEASHED (2) attached pets, use_leash obtains an adjacent location, finds a visible tame solid monster with limbs or a head that is not already leashed, and use_leash_core attaches the leash. Other use_leash_core branches handle invisible or unspotted targets, non-tame monsters, invalid forms, and detaching an in-use leash.
functions: leashable (pure predicate; rejects long worms, unsolid forms, and forms with neither limbs nor a head)
use_leash (returns ECMD_OK/ECMD_TIME; handles swallowed state, capacity, direction selection, mounted-self target, and absent/selected monster)
use_leash_core (void helper; handles visibility, tame state, attach eligibility, and detach/cursed cases)
doapply (LEASH switch arm consumes use_leash’s ECMD result)
callers: cmd.c command table maps apply command key a to doapply; js/cmd.js:runApplyCommand dispatches the JavaScript apply command to doapply(state).
apply.c:doapply LEASH arm calls use_leash(obj); use_leash calls use_leash_core for the selected monster, or for the steed when applying downward while mounted.
dependencies: get_adjacent_loc’s Boolean result and selected coordinate determine cancellation and target selection; number_leashed’s result is compared with MAXLEASHED=2 before attaching an unused leash.
u_at, m_at, and canspotmon determine hero/monster targeting and the spotmon argument; use_leash_core also checks the target tile’s invisible glyph.
unsolid, nolimbs, has_head, and leashable determine whether the leash fits. leashable is pure and needs source-pinned predicate tests if implemented.
The successful attach writes mtmp->mleashed=1 and obj->leashmon=mtmp->m_id together, clears mtmp->msleeping, and calls update_inventory; detach also clears both fields together and updates inventory.
unmap_invisible’s return is discarded in the empty-square branch; map_invisible is a void visibility side effect. set_bknown is used only by cursed-detach refusal.
mleashed_next2u/next_to_u later read the paired monster state when leaving a level; this selected recording ends immediately after attachment and does not exercise that downstream path.

evidence: Source: nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:758-883 defines MAXLEASHED, pure leashable, use_leash, and the full use_leash_core branch tree. The successful branch requires an unused leash, available leash capacity, a selected adjacent visible tame monster not already leashed, a solid form with limbs or a head, and a species accepted by leashable; it emits the slip-leash message, links the monster and leash IDs, wakes the monster, then updates inventory.

Source: nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:4297-4298 dispatches case LEASH through res = use_leash(obj), so use_leash’s ECMD result is consumed by doapply while use_leash_core’s void result is discarded. nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:1677-1678 maps command a to doapply.
